title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: When the Unkindled One arrives before the prince, he's welcomed by a bitter comment from Lothric, naming them as nothing but another fool attempting to win his favour or to take his life. The feathers covering every corner of the room indicate that the Winged Knights had tried to reach the Prince to either persuade or kill him, but were all eliminated by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian. Lothric then watches as Lorian engages the Unkindled One in combat, who defeats the elder prince. Teleporting next to his brother's body, Lothric revives Lorian and climbs onto his back, kindling their bodies together. The brothers then fight the Unkindled One as one, but are unable to overcome their enemy and are both cut down. As he dies, Lothric warns the Unkindled One that they would remain among the accursed.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Deacons of the Deep
snippet: When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. title: Lothric
snippet: As the kingdom of Lothric found itself managing the system of Firelinking,**** coupled with their subscription to the Way of Blue faith, it inevitably came into contact with Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Ruled by Gwyndolin, the king of the gods, Irithyll and Lothric recognized a common ground in their Firelinking legacy, as well as their faith which venerated the moon god. Soon after, the two kingdoms established diplomatic relations: the scholars and knights of Lothric would travel to Irithyll, and Lothric knights would adopt crossbows that used lightning bolts produced by the giant blacksmiths of Anor Londo. The Boreal Valley also became a place of pilgrimage for the knights of Lothric, who sought to reach the residence of their patron deity in Archdragon Peak through meditation.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: His decision shattered the realm, and as a plague of Pus of Man ravaged the city, a civil war erupted within Lothric's walls. The government of the Three Pillars, represented by Emma and the Knights, was trying to keep the kingdom together and still attempting to convince Lothric to reconsider his position and link the fading flame. On the other side, the Winged Knights, a portion of the army still heralding the royal insignia, was now clashing openly against the government, as they had embraced the heretical "Angelic Faith" spread by Gertrude. The scholars of the Archives apparently decided to ignore the situation and closed the doors of their facilities, isolating themselves to continue their studies.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: The king married the future Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric, with whom he conceived the divine princes of the kingdom.Lorian, the crown prince, received the ancient brass armor handed down by the royal family, complete with a crown patterned with flame, symbolic of the kingdom's tradition of Firelinking. Lorian was raised as a knight and proved his incredible prowess on the battlefield, leading a war against the remnants of the Chaos Demons, even capturing some of them to serve the kingdom as slaves. Lorian went on to face the Demon Prince, defeating him single-handedly in a battle that eternally scorched his greatsword with the flame of chaos and stained his armor black.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: In the last days of Lothric, as the First Flame was almost faded, flocks of Pilgrim Butterflies would manifest in the Lothric skies. These gigantic humanoid insects with immense, branch-like wings would infest the skies of the dying kingdom, migrating towards the tip of Lothric Castle. Here they would take control of the statue of a Dragonslayer Armour through dark magic, using it as a puppet to eliminate anyone who attempted to proceed to the top of the castle.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight was the Queen of Lothric and conceiving Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince, the younger son destined to link the First Flame. However, after Lothric refused to fulfill his duty, King Oceiros became obsessed with the power of dragons . Gwynevere granted his wish for an heir of divine and draconic blood and gave birth to her last children Ocelotte, however she later abandoned the kingdom of Lothric and quietly disappeared .

Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, still remains in the Ringed City, asleep to keep the city outside the flow of time and space. Shira, Knight of Filianore, daughter of Seath, continues to remain at her side, defending the princess's sleep and maintaining control over the noble Pygmy family.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric appears much more frail, and has noticeably dark veins, indicative of his disease, but still speaks as royalty with a formal and cold tone. Though shorter than his brother, he is still twice as tall as the Ashen One. He wears a black robe with golden decorations. During the second phase he will teleport down and hold on to his brother's back, using an unfamiliar holy light energy that functions like crystal sorceries of the highest level.

title: Lothric
snippet: At one point, a champion with an armor modelled after a king, Gundyr, was charged with linking the First Flame. Bestowed with an iron halberd which would never crumble, Champion Gundyr was sent to the Firelink Shrine to fulfill his duty. However, the champion found himself restrained by a chain that blocked him in his path, and he fell into an Abyss, getting lost in the folds of time. In this strange realm, the Firelink Shrine had no fire, and Gundyr ended up arriving "late" for the celebrations that awaited his fate. The Fire Keeper who was supposed to welcome her champion never met him, with the ensuing tragic farce becoming a favorite tale of the masses of Lothric, a stain on the reputation of future kings of the realm. However, the fate of Gundyr was not by chance, as the one who had charged him with his duty had also condemned him to eternal service from the beginning. title: Sister Friede
snippet: Following Prince Lothric's refusal to link the First Flame, the Unkindled were exhumed from their graves, tasked with hunting down the Lords of Cinder that had refused to serve once again as kindling. Among the resurrected Unkindled was Elfriede, who instead chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Left without a home, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where the forlorn and the outcast were welcomed and found refuge. Friede became the first Ashen One to reside in it, coming to accept the cold of the Painted World and considering it her new home. She discovered that she wanted to "protect" the inhabitants of the Painted World, and thus assumed the precise form that they yearned for: that of their former mistress Priscilla. title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - plot 
 plot : By the times of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, the destined Lord of Cinder of his generation, has refused to link the First Flame. This led to the resurrection of four Lords of Cinder of the past, whose conjoined, withered embers could kindle the First Flame in Lothric's stead. Aldrich, Saint of the Deep; Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Ludleth of Courland were expected to sacrifice themselves as kindling once again. When all Lords except Ludleth rejected this duty, the Unkindled too were resurrected as a last resort, who were fated to seek out the Lords (including Prince Lothric) and bring them back to their thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once the cinders of the Lords were restored to their thrones, an Unkindled champion would be bestowed the embers of the First Flame that remained within their cinders, and finally sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to complete their journey.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet: When the link of fire was threatened, the Lords of Cinder would be exhumed from their graves to once again serve as kindling for the First Flame. Ludleth was among those resurrected; though unlike the other three Lords, he accepted the call, and took up his throne at Firelink Shrine to await his fate.

title: Gods
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince, oldest two sons of Oceiros and Gwynevere when the latter was Queen of Lothric. Lorian was raised to inherit his father's throne, while Lothric was raised to become a Lord of Cinder; however, Lothric was born frail and weak, leading Lorian to join their souls together in an attempt to assist his brother. Ultimately, Lothric refused to Link the First Flame altogether.

title: Queen of Lothric
snippet: Analyzing the Queen of Lothric's behavior also shows very little overlap with that of the Gwynevere established within the same game. The Princess of Sunlight is characterized as a kind, loving figure who was cherished and adored in turn. A great mother who raised each of her children with love, remembered fondly to the very end. In contrast, the Queen of Lothric willingly married into a family bent on creating the perfect sacrifice and eager to do anything in order to achieve that. She gave life to Lothric just so he may one day be used as kindling, without even raising him herself but handing him off to a wet nurse instead. She did nothing when her own daughter was imprisoned and left to wither away in a cell, and also abandoned her newborn son with her maddened husband.

 firelinking_duty : The tradition of linking the Flame plays a central role in Lothric, testified by the Firelink Shrine's location just outside the city walls, connected to the Royal Gardens. A large number of people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual initiated by Lord Gwyn's sacrifice. Those who failed, becoming the Unkindled, were buried near the Shrine in the Cemetery of Ash. Next to the Cemetery was an arena complete with stands, where Iudex Gundyr's golem judged those who aspired to become Lords, testing their strength. The ritual of the linking of the Flame permeated the kingdom at every level up to the royal family, who were obsessed with producing a worthy Champion in their line to preserve their divine mandate as the guardians of the Age of Fire.

title: Lothric
snippet: Due to the Convergence, a massive seismic upheaval raised the Lothric plateau high above the land, cutting it off from its neighbouring regions. This new feature was called the High Wall, and removed all means of transportation in or out of the city. Lothric messengers had no means of returning, and pilgrims of Londor were unable to seek refuge, leading to the total isolation of the kingdom during its final days. The Stray Demon that was once the gatekeeper of Lothric would remain trapped on the kingdom's broken bridge, without even a trace of its flame.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Lothric is a pale, emaciated young humanoid of great size. He has long, claw-like fingers, light-colored hair that falls to his shoulders, and dark, sunken eyes. The way he clings to Lorian's back during battle suggests he is unable to walk due to his illness. He wears the same baby clothes that he used throughout his entire life. Lothric relies on magic alone during battle, and is a considerably powerful magic user, casting homing soul masses, soul spears, and teleporting his brother around the arena. He is one of the few humanoid magic users in the series to cast spells without any apparent catalyst.

snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. However, most Lords refused the call to action, with Aldrich denouncing his throne based on an epiphany: that an Age of Deep would soon be cast upon the world. The Cathedral had by then become a shrine to unspeakable horrors, to all repulsive rejects that sought a cure in its cleansing waters. The Ashen One defeats the Dancer and reaches Lothric Castle, the highest point of the city and fights their way through knights of opposing factions and wyverns

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Lothric
snippet: The new inhabitants of the region soon found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. The old knights of Lothric turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, and built an altar for him in their city, beginning to worship the ancient deity who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Queen of Lothric
snippet:
Queen of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Queen of Lothric was the latest matriarch of the titular kingdom. She was wed to King Oceiros, and likened to the goddess of fertility and bounty.

She delivered three scions to the royal bloodline during her time as queen. The first of them was Lorian, a boy raised to be a knight, who grew up into a hero and found glory battling the Demons and defeating their Prince in combat. The second one was Lothric, a sickly boy born to be a Lord of Cinder, left for High Priestess Emma to raise. The last one was Ocelotte, a mysterious child of dragons whose birth caused the Queen's equally mysterious disappearance.

These were not her only children, however. The Queen of Lothric had a holy maiden who was also her direct offspring, while sharing no blood relation with Lothric's royal family. Whether she had the child before her marriage with Oceiros or during it is not clarified.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : When the player enters the throne room, they will view a cutscene where Lothric, Younger Prince addresses them, stating his disdain for his duty to become a Lord of Cinder. During this Lorian, Elder Prince, will crawl from the shadows and prepare to fight the Ashen One.

The battle will begin with the player facing Lorian alone. While Lorian is crippled below the waist and has trouble moving by himself, he is aided by Lothric, who will use his magic to teleport Lorian around the arena, whether it is to a blind spot to the player's side or away to allow him to use his special attacks. All of Lorian's attacks deal moderate damage and inflict Fire damage, and he has numerous combos that can add up to quickly kill unwary players.

title: Angel
snippet: As the pilgrims of Londor were sent to Lothric with the objective to die some of them died and turned into "angels". One day one of them managed to visit Gertrude, the holy maiden of Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric and it revealed to her a truth capable of manifesting pillars of light together with a heretic tale. The holy maiden was convinced by this enlightenment and began to spread the worship of those she considered "divine messengers". However this faith was viewed as heresy in Lothric, as it opposed the worship of the ancient gods and the duty to continue linking the First Flame and was consequently unrecognized by any of the Three Pillars that govern the realm, leading to a civil war inside the walls of Lothric between the Winged Knights that followed Gertrude's faith and the Angels and those still loyal to the Pillars.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world had become irreparably corrupted, and all lands from all previous points in time had begun to converge upon a single point: the Kingdom of Lothric. Upon reviving and seeing what had become of the world they had fought to protect, the Lords of Cinder, too, rejected the linking of the Flame and refused to sit upon their thrones. Aldrich, one of the Lords of Cinder, decided not to take his throne after experiencing visions of the deep sea and its inevitable coming.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Oceiros created immense propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance. In a betrayal of the hopes placed in him, Lothric remained a sick and shriveled child from birth into adulthood, never even growing out of his baby clothes, which remained his only clothing throughout his life and were blessed to at least try to keep him healthy. In his youth, Aldia, the first of the Grand Archives scholars, became his mentor in secret, a likely influence on the young and impressionable prince, with whom he would have imparted his skepticism on the nature of the Age of Fire.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: In the final days of Lothric, the citizens of the kingdom forgot even the miracles of the goddess of sunlight, and ended up recounting childish but earnest stories to try to recall her blessings and the back of her figure, as the last image of their queen before she left.

As a proof of this, not only other identical knights can be found in in the Consumed King's Garden, with the only difference of the former ones wearing blue robes and tunics, as the distinct colour of the Royal Family's Guard in Lothric, but their own shields are decorated with "an emblem of an old king of Lothric". This testifies the strong connection and alliance that linked Lothric with the Way of White and the government of Anor Londo (Irithyll) before Prince Lothric renouced his role as Lord of Cinder and despised the link of fire, but it also tells about how great and spreaded was the concern of the Cathedral getting increasingly swallowed and corrupted by the Depths: so much that Lothric's king decided to send a regiment of his personal guard to keep the order

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: After her father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, in a betrayal of his father's legacy, chose to ally with the dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. She abandoned Anor Londo along with most other deities and moved to an unknown location. Sometime after her departure she married Flame God Flann.

title: Londor
snippet: close_of_an_age_of_fire : As the First Flame faded and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Unkindled were exhumed from their graves to hunt down the Lords of Cinder of the past that had refused to return to their "thrones" and serve as fuel for the Flame a second time. It was at this pivotal moment that Londor and the Sable Church decided to make their move. Hundreds of Hollows were exiled from Londor, sent away to Lothric on a pilgrimage with the specific goal of "dying". They were equipped with shell-shaped protections chained to their backs, similar to ones found on robes of clerics that warded off stagnant darkness during long journeys which could manifest as Pus of Man. Finally these pilgrims were taught a dark miracle, the only tale known to them, that they believed carried words of forgiveness; in reality they were cursed by this magic, which attracted more attention from foes, and presumably accelerated their "preordained death".

title: The Nameless King
snippet: In the heyday of Lothric, when the descendants of Drangleic and followers of the Way of Blue and the Heirs of the Sun moved to another location, they still remembered the Nameless King as their God of the Sun. As the early inhabitants of Lothric found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns, they had to become dragonslayers to survive; and so they turned to the Nameless King, building an altar for him. The first knights of Lothric devoted themselves to the worship of the ancestral deity of the sun and war, who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The lands of the old empire of Drangleic begin to move towards the First Flame, into a region that will one day be called Lothric
The old people of Lothric find themselves in a region full of Wyverns
The old knights of Lothric are founded upon dragonslaying
The old knights of Lothric receive the influence of the Ornstein's knights in the forging of their armor
The old knights of Lothric receive the influence of Anor Londo's culture, forging axes made for beheading dragons
The old knights of Lothric welcome Forossa's knights in their ranks
The old knights of Lothric follow the cult of Gwyn's firstborn
The old knights of Lothric build a shrine to Gwyn's firstborn in their barracks
The old knights of Lothric learn how to use lightning to hunt dragons from Gwyn's firstborn
The number of wyverns infesting the region's skies is reduced
Among the ranks of the old knights of Lothric a king emerges
The city of Lothric is built

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: Considering that those who had deceived Gundyr had given him his halberd and charged him with linking the Flame, they must have had a position superior to the king of Lothric but still close to him. This could point to the involvement of Gwyndolin, king of the gods of Irithyll, who had strong ties to Lothric; or the Primordial Serpents, who were already advisors to the royal family. Using Gundyr as a golem to test the strength of future Champions would ensure that those overseeing the linking of the Flame would be guaranteed to find potential Lords with enough power to prolong the Age of Fire.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Timeline
snippet:
An old armor of the ancient dragonslayers remains as a monument near the city barracks
The kingdom of Lothric builds an incredible army of skilled knights assisted by the wyverns they were able to tame
The kingdom of Lothric annihilates every other kingdom that drifts on its borders for centuries
---Lothric's knight become dragon worshipper---

title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Before the Lord of Sunlight sacrificed himself to link the First Flame, he divided his power among his family, instructed his sons to lead humanity and passed down his sunlight and title to his firstborn. However, his son would eventually be exiled and erased from history due to his actions, and taking advantage of the situation, Lloyd would proclaim himself "Allfather", leader of all the other gods and main figure of the Way of White. His claim remained unopposed, despite his grandnephew Gwyndolin having a stronger case for inheriting the position seeing as it was the religion of Gwyn's immediate family. Sadly, the reclusive god still viewed himself as repulsive and unworthy of his father's legacy and the task he had bestowed upon him.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet: Given how the firstborn only had respect for arms, it's possible that he chose to ally with the dragons, hence why the Gods would expunge him from history. It is known that the firstborn left the Sunlight Blade Miracle on Gwyn's honorary tomb in Anor Londo as a final farewell, which could only mean that Gwyn had already departed for the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet: At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the deities abandoned Anor Londo and moved to an unknown location. Ornstein seemingly remained in the forsaken city alongside Executioner Smough to guard the cathedral where Gwynevere, the Princess of Sunlight resided.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The Ashen One reaches the High Wall of Lothric and fights their way through the now hollow soldiers and citizens of the city and reaches the cathedral of Lothric
The Ashen One is welcomed by Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle, who reveals to them that the Lords of Cinder are not in Lothric and that they will have to look for them in the lands where they returned, indicating that they begin their journey from the base of the High Walls
The Ashen One reaches the gate of the Walls of Lothric but finds their way blocked by Vordt of the Boreal Valley, a monstrous knight from Irithyll patrolling the access
The Ashen One defeats Vordt and is able to descend from the Wall, finding themselves on the broken bridge that once led to Lothric
The Ashen One meets Yoel of Londor, a pilgrim from Londor, on the broken bridge and accepts him into their service as a sorcerer

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: After his father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, treacherously, chose to "ally" with the ancient dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. Following these events, his sister Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities, leaving Gwyndolin as the last remaining deity in the city. Despite being the last son of the royal family of the gods, Gwyndolin was psychologically unfit to become the next ruler, still playing the feminine role imposed on him by his father Gwyn, leaving Lloyd to take advantage of the situation who proclaimed himself king of the gods, justified by his being Gwyn's uncle, and become the chief deity of the Way of White.

title: Sen's Fortress
snippet: Centuries after Lord Gwyn's sacrifice, as the First Flame began to fade and the curse of Undeath to regain strength heroes and warriors from all different lands tried to reach Lordran and ventured to Sen's Fortress to try and reach Anor Londo. Very few were successful, like the strongest Berenike Knight known as Black Iron Tarkus and a Warrior of Sunlight known as Solaire of Astora. However, most of them failed in their mission to conquer the fortress's challenges despite their multiple attempts over the decades, ending up trapped, hollow or only became additional roadblocks to further hinder future warriors.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: also be found within Lothric Castle. It's important to note that Lothric and Irithyll remained on good terms even after Sulyvahn's coup, with the Pontiff sending Gargoyles from the Profaned Capital to the Grand Archives, and Grand Archives Scholars travelling to Irithyll. The path to the Archdragon Peak is situated in Irithyll Dangeons, and many Lothric knights are bowed near the Dragon Torso Stone, implying that the knights went in pilgrimage to the Peak, and the fact that they were left untouched by the Jailers is a proof that Lothric was allied with the Pontiff.

title: Humans
snippet: Over time, others would repeat Gwyn's sacrifice—either for their own reasons or to follow in his footsteps—to rekindle the First Flame. As the First Flame was not intended to burn as long as it had, the fabric of reality began to suffer.

title: Gertrude
snippet: In the final days of the reign of Lothric and the First Flame, Gertrude died, still in her cage, surrounded by feathers and clutching onto her writings. The Winged Knights continue to patrol various locations within Lothric and the Castle, and Gertrude's most loyal Knights, who managed to develop large feathered wings, remain positioned to defend their saint's resting place.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Whatever the Angels communicated to Gertrude might have been the announcement of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of the Age of Dark, justifying the Kingdom's violent reaction. Given that Lothric culture essentially evolved around Firelinking, the Three Pillars had a stake in denouncing the revelations of the Angels who traced their roots to Londor, a realm devoted to bringing about an Age of Dark. Furthermore, the apparent ability of the Angel's miracle being able to manifest "light", counterintuitive to the Angels' somber origins, could have suggested that a world without flame would not be as "dark" as the Three Pillars would have Lothric believe.

title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
By the events of *Dark Souls III*, however, the flame is dying and the Demons are as well. The Stray Demon lacks any flame whatsoever.

Though it was not successful in replacing the First Flame, it functions similarly to it, as Demons can become powerful enough to "link" it and rekindle it when it dies out. The chosen one for this task was the Demon Prince, whose will is within all Demonkind, but his defeat at the hands of Prince Lorian of Lothric, and later the Ashen One, left the demon race without a champion, rendering them extinct.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: Ages after her Lord Soul was used to link the First Flame, Izalith's very name was lost. In the region of Drangleic, only few remained who remembered her—only that she was the mother of pyromancy, and that she was devoured by her chaos flame. However, some remnants of her soul manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick fled the Castle through the King's Passage never to return, fearing Nashandra's wickedness. He left the Looking Glass Knight behind him, ready to expunge those who would challenge him, forever true to his original command, as the first line of defense against those who would attempt to pursue the runaway king into the Undead Crypt. The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Here, left alone, he isolated himself in a secluded room wearing only his robes, crown, sword and his ring. Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon

title: Untended Graves
snippet:
Untended Graves -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : This location is sealed away from the eye of everyone, hidden in secret within the deepest parts of Lothric's castle: it shows a time, in the past of Lothric, when the Fire almost faded completely, and with the light nearly eradicated, time has stagnated to the point where past, present and future co-exist. That is the reason why Gundyr is not yet "Iudex", "judge of the ash": Gundyr was a champion who "came too late" and was "greeted by a shrine without fire, and a bell that would not toll.". He was bested by an unknown warrior and became the sheath of a Coiled Sword, in the hopes that someday, the first flame would be linked once more.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
With Elfriede at the helm, the Sable Church developed dark miracles, forged specialized weaponry, and trained knights unflinchingly loyal to their cause. The influence of the Sable Church would extend beyond Londor and into other realms via Londor Pale Shades, assassins and knights who served the interests of the Church abroad. At some point, Sir Vilhelm would come under the employ of the three sisters of the Church. He was especially loyal to Elfriede, becoming her steadfast follower and cold-blooded hangman.

Elfriede eventually departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, realizing Kaathe's vision of an Age of Dark, or wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose. Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The remnants of the will and power of Gwyn, as the first one to ever link the First Flame, would emerge as part of the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame throughout history, thus creating a hollowed-out entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions.

The powers of Gwyn would manifest when the Soul of Cinder was challenged by an aspiring Champion; acting as the Flame's last line of defense within the Kiln, the Soul of Cinder fought to either test the might of one who would link the Flame, or to protect it from a would-be betrayer or usurper.

title: The Deep
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their humanity, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder—just for his strength, without regard for his morality. Now left to indulge in his perversions so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: It was not chance that bound him to this fate, however: The one who had charged him with his duty had also condemned him to eternal service from the beginning. Imprisoned, Gundyr was defeated by an unknown warrior and became sheath to a coiled sword. Transformed into an indestructible golem, he became the ritual test of strength for those who would attempt to link the First Flame after him. Over time an arena complete with stands was built around his remains, in which the now Iudex Gundyr would "judge" those who aspired to become Lords.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - lead 
 lead : The **Unkindled** or are "nameless, accursed Undead" who tried to link the First Flame and become Lords of Cinder, being mighty enough to reach the Kiln of the First Flame but ultimately perishing there, their quest ending in failure.

title: Demon Prince
snippet:
Demon Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Chaos Flame, like the First Flame that it was unable to replace, is capable of being rekindled by a champion demon of vast power. Such a so-called "prince" went to face Lorian, eldest son of the Lothric royal family, and was defeated in combat. But the race of demons shares memory with each other, and those that remembered the power and determination of the Demon Prince share in this essence, so that even the last demon alive can rekindle the Chaos Flame.

At the end of the Age of Fire, reality has partially collapsed onto itself, gathering all lands onto one point of convergence. At the bottom of a large tree rest two demons, the last demons by that time, and the last one to survive shall be reborn as the Demon Prince.

title: Crown of the Great Lord
snippet:
Crown of the Great Lord -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : Crown of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his great clan before linking the flame. But he did keep his crown, perhaps to preserve a symbol of the monarch, for its actual power had fully subsided.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Soul of Cinder: A deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history.
Yhorm the Giant: A giant humanoid, king of the Profaned Capital, who linked the First Flame in an attempt to save his city from the Profaned Flame.
Ludleth of Courland: A small pygmy from Courland and a student of the art of transposition: the process of extracting and coalescing the essence of souls to gain incredible powers.
Abyss Watchers: A legion of Undead soldiers tasked with fighting the Abyss wherever it takes shape, united in their souls by the wolf blood of Artorias to link the First Flame and do their duty one last time.
Aldrich, Saint of the Deep: A cleric from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley who took pleasure in devouring humans, eating so much that his body became a sludge of darkness and was made to link the First Flame for his strength.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Gods
snippet:
Lord Gwyn, God of Sunlight, who claimed a Lord Soul, conquered the world after defeating the Dragons and ruled it as king of the Gods. He eventually sacrificed himself to Link the First Flame, becoming the first Lord of Cinder, with his empty husk guarding the Flame. He is regarded as the omnipotent main deity of the Way of White, the faith worshipping the Gods of Anor Londo.
Gwyn's Firstborn Son, once a God of War and of the Sun, who had originally inherited Gwyn's throne and ruled Anor Londo. However, he would later be cast out and stripped of his status as a deity, his faith becoming anathema to the Way of White while he became a nameless king, with all traces of him erased from history. He was succeeded by Lloyd as ruler of the Gods. His symbol is that of a sun.

title: Soul of the King
snippet:
Soul of the King -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : Soul of Vendrick, King of Drangleic. The King was wasted away, a shadow of his former self, but still held something dear.

Use the soul of he who would link the flame to acquire numerous souls, or create something of great worth.

title: Black Hand Gotthard
snippet:
Black Hand Gotthard -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : A hunter who served several kings of Lothric. He held the title of "Black Hand", a title that is only bestowed upon hunters that serve successive kings. To date, only three have obtained this title (Black Hand Kamui is one and the other is unknown).

He was able to obtain said title due to his expert swordsmanship. Eventually, due to the decaying state of the kingdom, he attempted to escape Lothric Castle, though he did not succeed. He wears the Black Hand Set, and wields the Gotthard Twinswords and a Composite Bow.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Timeline -  Dark Souls III - storyline - dark_souls_iii_the_last_days_of_the_fire 
 dark_souls_iii_the_last_days_of_the_fire : (The events before Dark Souls III)

Over the centuries, dozens of people link themselves to the First Flame, becoming Lords of Cinder
The souls of all those who have linked the First Flame manifest in the form of the Soul of Cinder, an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Lords of Cinder even if it's just an empty husk.
This manifestation of the previous Lords of Cinder exists as the First Flame's last defense from future linkers
The future Lords of Cinder face the Soul of Cinder at the Kiln of the First Flame before they can link the First Flame

Due to the First Flame naturally dying out, time and space slowly converge towards it, bringing the various regions of the world towards the Kiln of the First Flame

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - grand_archives_and_prince_lothric 
 grand_archives_and_prince_lothric : Progressing through Lothric Castle will bring the Ashen One face to face with a Dragonslayer Armour controlled by a Pilgrim Butterfly. Defeating the armour opens the way to the Grand Archives, home to ancient knowledge.

The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

title: The Deep
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Aldrich denounced this call to action based on an epiphany: that an **Age of Deep** would soon be cast upon the world. The Cathedral had by then become a shrine to unspeakable horrors, to all repulsive rejects that once sought a cure in its cleansing waters. Within the Cathedral—in McDonnell's sorceries, and their taboo miracles— Aldrich observed a stagnation that seemed inherent to the world, belike rotten remains which find their way down into a dark, deep seabed. Following these ruminations on the nature of existence, Aldrich concluded that an Age of Deep was what followed the waning Age of Fire. He understood that all things would stagnate into the Deep, including the representatives of the old world order; he also understood that he was in a position where he could help usher in the new Age. Thus he set out to

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn ordered the Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight, equivalent to being exiled. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given the eye rings of the Pontiff, which eventually transformed them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, which ensured Sulyvahn's total control over the knights and deprived them of any means of desertion.

The Dancer was sent to Lothric together with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma. Like other Outrider Knights, she would end up transformed into a frenzied beast by the rings of the Pontiff, causing her armor to be fused with her hide.

title: Soul Stream
snippet:
Soul Stream -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : Sorcery imparted by the first of the Scholars, when Lothric and the Grand Archives were but young.

Fires a torrential volley of souls.

The first of the Scholars doubted the linking of the fire, and was alleged to be a private mentor to the Royal Prince.

title: Flynn
snippet:
Flynn -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the times and region of Lothric, Flynn was still known as a gentleman thief. He still fought with the wind's blessing on his side, and was celebrated by the poor and the weak. But regardless of this admiration, those who looked up to him ultimately believed he would not come to aid them, and that it was all merely a fantasy to imagine the contrary. The reason why that is isn't touched upon, leaving the thief's fate up in the air; he either perished and faded to mere legend, or left for parts unknown.

title: Winged Knight Helm
snippet:
Winged Knight Helm -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Armor of the Winged Knights, who swore themselves to the Angels.

Worship of the divine messengers was viewed as heresy in Lothric and unrecognized by any of the Three Pillars of rule.

This is believed to be why Gertrude, the Heavenly Daughter, was imprisoned in the lofty cell of the Grand Archives.

title: Black Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Black Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : Former Silver Knights loyal to Lord Gwyn who tragically were burned, their armors ending up charred, in their expedition to the Kiln of the First Flame in Gwyn's desperate attempt to link the flame.

title: Demon Prince
snippet:
Demon Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - demon_prince 
 demon_prince : The Demon Prince uses different abilities depending on which of the demons from the first phase was killed last. If the Demon from Below (the orange demon) was killed last and becomes the Demon Prince, he will cast Seething Chaos on occasion and uses a long-duration laser ray ability which is easily avoided by staying close to him, allowing the player to inflict free damage while the laser is being fired. If the Demon in Pain (the red demon) was killed last, the Demon Prince can cast Floating Chaos and charge up a powerful aerial maelstrom that releases a large number of highly-damaging meteors into the arena when completed.

title: Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild
snippet:
Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Kriemhild was set to become a Fire Keeper, but instead became the Crystal Sages' favorite student and was even gifted with one of their crystal spheres fixed into a staff.

After Lothric refused to link the flame, Kriemhild decided to protect him from any Flame contender, in order to let the Age of Dark come.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Following the failure of this first contingency plan, a second plan is activated: Unkindled, those who had previously tried to link the First Flame but who had failed to do so, are resurrected from their graves in the Cemetery of Ash, and tasked with placing the rebellious Lords of Cinder upon their thrones so that the First Flame might be linked once more. The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: After his father Gwyn left to link the First Flame, the throne of Anor Londo would pass to the eldest son of the King; and so the Nameless King inherited the Sunlight of his father. He would thus wear the golden crown, and succeed his father's titles of "king of the gods" and "god of the sun". The Nameless King was said to be inferior to none in terms of military strength. Gwyn's firstborn preserved his father's design and instructions, shepherding humans on the path to the Linking of the First Flame to continue the Age of Fire. In fact, underneath Anor Londo, a city was built exclusively for the undead, with an altar inside for the firstborn of Gwyn, and the aim of guiding a chosen undead who would one day sacrifice themselves to the Flame. Inside the city was the Undead Parish, a church at the center of the cult of the burg and connected to the first test to start on the path of Firelinking and ring the first Bell of Awakening. Furthermore, the town was connected to the Firelink

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Soul of Cinder is the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history, becoming Lords of Cinder, and thus is an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions despite just being an empty husk.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

When tested by an aspiring Champion, the Soul of Cinder would even bring out the remnants of the will and power of the first one to ever link the First Flame: Lord Gwyn himself.

Gundyr drifted into a moment of time when the Firelink Shrine had no fire and ended up arriving "late" for the celebrations that awaited his fate. The Fire Keeper who was supposed to welcome her champion never met him and the ensuing tragic farce became a favorite tale of the masses of Lothric, a stain on the reputation of the realm.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

 characteristics : Lorian's Set is on the lighter end of the heavy armor sets, and as such, the defenses provided are not as robust as its heavier cousins.

Despite having respectable physical defenses, it is exceedingly weak to Strike damage, moreso than is usually the case for plate metal sets. Its elemental resistances are on the unorthodox side, being resistant to Magic and Dark damage much like the Sunless Set but being unusually weak to Fire damage alongside Lightning. Its resistance to status effects is rather unusual, as it is fairly well-rounded outside of its intolerance to Poison buildup.

It possesses a rather poor poise-to-weight ratio, making it closer in protection to medium armor sets than to heavy sets. This makes it rather weak for trading against other large weapons, even when wielding an Ultra Greatsword.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
The best way to fight Lorian is to always stay near him, giving him no opportunity to teleport to close the distance and attack the player from blind angles. Beware that using greatswords and larger is not recommended, as their long animations will give Lorian ample time to counter. Try to get in one or two quick swings, and then prepare to roll to dodge Lorian's retaliations.

During the second phase, the player must defeat Lothric by getting behind Lorian during his attacks and striking Lothric directly. Depending on the weapon being used, Lothric may take less damage than Lorian from attacks that hit them both; Lothric is weak to slash and thrust damage, so weapons like katanas or thrusting swords may work well. However, Lothric also has almost twice as much health as Lorian, so it is very difficult to avoid a situation where Lothric can be defeated without felling Lorian at least once.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: ***Plunging Attack**: Sometimes, before executing the overhead part of his three-slash combo, Lorian will teleport away. When he emerges, it will be right above the player, where he will bring the sword down in a plunging attack. This attack can usually be predicted by the teleportation circle appearing extremely close to the player but with nothing emerging from it on the ground, indicating that Lorian is above them. The best course of action is to immediately roll away, as the plunge has a narrow hitbox and predictable timing. Lorian will take some time to recover from this, allowing the player to get some attacks in.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
As with the first phase, it is best to try to stay relatively close to the Twin Princes, as this gives Lothric less opportunity to cast his ranged spells. Bait Lorian's attacks, then roll in behind him and strike at Lothric whenever possible.

When Lorian falls, try to deal as much damage to Lothric as possible, but be ready to immediately retreat in order to avoid the area-of-effect knockback that occurs when he revives Lorian. There is a short period of time when Lothric is getting back on Lorian's back where he is vulnerable to attacks, so be ready to rush in once the resurrection spell is complete. Each time he is revived, Lorian will have less health, however the quickest path to victory is to try to defeat Lothric before he can revive Lorian more than once.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: ***Teleport**: Lothric will teleport Lorian around the battle arena, allowing Lorian to quickly bring his attacks to bear on the player or to attack them from a blind spot to the player's side or back. When this happens, it is important to read Lorian's tell right before he disappears, because *he will always resume his attack with that tell when he emerges*, allowing players to predict which attack he will use after a short delay. This means that with good timing, even attacks from behind the player can be predicted and dodged with good rolling. Additionally, whenever the player enters the arena beyond the first encounter, Lorian will often greet the player with a teleporting attack, but will not do so if the player does not move away from the entrance fog for the first few seconds of the fight.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: lothric_younger_prince : ***Holy Homing Soulmass**: Lothric will wave his left arm, sending several white orbs into the air; he will always begin the second phase with this attack. After a short period of time, they will become active and home in on the player. They do not do much damage individually and have poor staggering potential, however they can quickly rack up damage if multiple orbs hit, especially if the player is also busy trying to avoid Lorian's sword swings. Lothric will usually cast this if the player tries to retreat to create distance. It is best to try to create some moderate distance away from the Twin Princes while dodging the orbs, but not so far as to trigger the teleportation. Try to bait Lorian into performing some sword swings, and then retreat out of range so that he cannot perform another attack while you are dodging the orbs. These orbs can be blocked by the pillars at the sides of the room.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Whenever Lorian teleports, keep an eye on his tells to see which attack he was about to perform. When he emerges after a short delay, he will resume with that attack. Good timing means that no matter where Lorian attacks from, whether it is in front of or behind the player, a roll can be executed to avoid damage. As well, keep in mind that when entering the arena via fog door after the first encounter, Lorian will always start by teleporting near the player and attack. However, if the player remains in place as they enter, when he teleports, he will end up doing so near his initial location, giving the player the option to start the encounter in a less compromising way.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : During the first phase, the player must defeat Lorian by dodging his attacks and attacking him during his recoveries. Good rolling is mandatory, as Lorian's attacks all deal extremely heavy damage and inflict Fire damage, meaning that even greatshields cannot completely mitigate damage. As Lorian's recovery windows are quite small, fast-swinging weapons such as straight swords are highly recommended in order to leave the player less vulnerable when Lorian begins attacking again.

Lorian is extremely weak to Lightning damage, so use of Gold Pine Resin or Lightning Blade can allow players to quickly pass through the first phase. As well, dealing enough damage to Lorian in a short amount of time will stagger him, allowing the player to riposte him from the front.

 description : Both brothers have lengthy gray silver hair, pale skin, similar to Irithyllians, and have lanky bodies.

Lorian is a knight with gold and black armor, armed with a flaming greatsword; his helmet has a crown-like design and covers his eyes, seemingly to no detriment. He is mute and crippled, with legs so weak that he is unable to stand upright for more than a second, requiring him to walk on his knees or crawl most of the time. He is extremely tall, with the Ashen One only barely passing his knees.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: ***Fire Wave**: Lorian will bring himself upright, holding his sword up to his right with both hands. He will then bring the sword down behind him and slash forward after a short delay, casting a wide wave of fire in front of him. The fire has moderate range and can be rolled through with good timing, or avoided entirely by being far enough away. Beware that the sword swing itself can also hit players, dealing heavy damage and launching them skyward.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: ***Holy Soul Spear**: Lothric will charge energy in his left hand, and then send forward a spear of white light that can deal moderate damage to the player. He will usually perform this attack when the player is out of immediate range of any of Lorian's attacks. It has predictable timing and can be easy to dodge, however it can interrupt players attempting to create distance to use Estus or cast a spell. Lothric always follows up on Lorian's Holy Ray with this attack, meaning that the player must roll twice. Note that he cannot hit the player if he is in melee range of Lorian, as he cannot aim his spell downwards enough.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
***Lunging Overhead**: If the player is in front of Lorian and not within immediate melee range, Lorian may quickly lunge forward and bring his sword down in an overhead slash. This attack has almost no tell (Lorian will lurch down slightly and bring his left hand to the ground), so quick reactions are necessary in order to avoid it. Lorian will often use this attack in an attempt to punish players who retreat away to drink Estus or cast a spell/buff, however it can be avoided by backing far enough away.
***Dropping Strike**: Lorian will raise himself to his feet, and then bring the weight of his whole body down on his sword into one powerful strike. As this attack is well-telegraphed, it can be reliably dodged by rolling to the side when he begins his fall. It is also possible to utilize invincibility frames to roll forward through the attack and end up near Lorian to attack him while he is recovering.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian's most powerful attack has him teleport away from the player, and then begin charging his sword with holy energy; after a few seconds, he will slam his sword into the ground and unleash a ray of light at the player, dealing extreme amounts of damage. As this attack is capable of killing players in a single hit, it is imperative to roll to avoid it at all costs.

Once Lorian has been felled, another cutscene will take place with Lothric coming down from his bedstead to aid his brother, reviving him and then climbing onto his back. The battle will then recommence, with the player facing the Twin Princes.

During the second phase, Lorian will possess the same abilities that he did before, however now he will be aided by Lothric, who adds his own attacks on top of Lorian's. These include a holy version of Homing Soulmass, as well as Soul Spear.

snippet: At some point, Gwynevere would leave Irithyll and reach Lothric to marry into the bloodline of its monarchs, becoming the queen of the kingdom. The goddess resumed her role as a divinity in the city, producing holy water with healing properties and being worshipped by the citizens as a symbol of "bounty and fertility".
